plan: With a private value of $13, my goal is to maximize potential profit. Since values are randomly drawn, I'll use a moderate bidding strategy. Bidding exactly my value ($13) risks losing money if others bid higher. I'll bid slightly below my value at $12.5 to create a buffer. This gives me a chance to win if others bid conservatively, while protecting some potential profit margin. The randomness means I can't perfectly predict others' bids, so a strategic, slightly conservative approach is best.

With a private value of $15, I want to maximize potential profit. Since values are drawn randomly between $0-$49, other bidders likely have values in similar range. My optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value to minimize potential loss. A bid around $14-$15 balances potential winning with risk management. I'll aim to win only if my bid is close to my actual value, protecting against overpaying.

With a high private value of $47, I want to win but avoid overpaying. Since values are randomly drawn, I'll use a strategic bid below my full value. Other bidders likely have values between $0-$49. A bid around $40-$45 balances winning probability with profit protection. I'll aim slightly above midpoint to signal serious intent but not reveal full value. My goal is positive expected value by winning without paying more than item's worth.
